description: Every automerge rule below deliberately leaves automergeType at its default, 'pr'.
Do not set it to 'branch'. A branch automerge pushes a Renovate branch with NO pull
request, and a repo whose required status checks trigger on `pull_request` therefore
never reports them on that branch — so branch protection can never be satisfied and
the update rebases nightly, forever. nicgpt lost six branches this way for up to 83
days (renovate/react, renovate/lock-file-maintenance, renovate/provider-runtime,
renovate/nextjs-monorepo, renovate/postcss-8.x, renovate/vitest), and the tell was
the dashboard's 'Pending Branch Automerge' section rather than any failure anywhere.
With 'pr', Renovate merges the PR itself once the branch is green, which works on
protected and unprotected repos alike — platformAutomerge stays off, see its commit.
The security fast-path. Until 2026-08-22 there was none: GitHub vulnerability
alerts were DISABLED on all 11 repos, so Renovate had no data source and could
not raise a security PR at all. A CVE therefore waited for the Monday window like
a cosmetic bump, and the nine `next` CVEs were fixed by a hand-rolled branch.
Alerts were enabled on all 11 repos on 2026-08-22; this block says what happens next.
schedule + minimumReleaseAge are overridden HERE deliberately: the Monday window and
the 7-day soak on next/react are right for routine bumps and wrong for a live CVE.
groupName below keeps the vitest packages in ONE security PR and leaves every other
security update exactly as it was. Ungrouping here is deliberate — one CVE per PR
lands the fix sooner — and it is wrong for a package whose new version needs a
newer peer than the repo has, because then the ungrouped PR cannot install at all.
An EXACT peer pin always does that, and it is the case this block handles.
@vitest/coverage-v8@4.1.11 requires vitest@4.1.11: no caret, no range. When
CVE-2026-84373 hit vitest on 2026-09-10 it pulled vitest out of the group and left
@vitest/coverage-v8 behind in the ordinary one, so the pair became two PRs that each
changed only package.json. Renovate could not regenerate either lockfile, npm ci
failed ERESOLVE, and ci / baseline-rebuild-local / Vercel went red with it on
nicgpt #330 + #333, el-ifs #59 + #62, health #30 and learn #301. The CVE fix was
unlandable for five days because the PR carrying it could not merge.
WHY A TEMPLATE AND NOT A PLAIN NAME. Renovate spreads this whole block into a
`force` object on the rule it generates per advisory (process/vulnerabilities.ts),
and config/utils.ts ends every mergeChildConfig with `{ ...config, ...config.force }`.
So whatever this block says beats every packageRule below, and the inherited default
of groupName: null is precisely what ungroups the pair. Three things that look like
fixes are not, and two of them validate clean while doing nothing:
- a plain string here ('vitest') groups EVERY security update in every repo under
that one name — lodash and next were seen landing on renovate/vitest;
- a nested packageRules entry setting groupName is overwritten back to null by
that same force object on the next merge;
- `force` inside such a rule is globalOnly (options/index.ts:562) and is stripped
from a repository config with a warning.
The template is what makes it narrow: it is compiled per update, so only the vitest
packages get a group name at all.
THE ELSE BRANCH IS LOAD-BEARING — DO NOT SHORTEN IT TO ''. It reproduces Renovate's
default vulnerability branchTopic byte for byte, so every other security branch is
untouched (verified: lodash, next, @types/node, axios, @babel/core and socket.io all
keep renovate/npm-<dep>-vulnerability, with identical PR titles). An empty string
would NOT turn grouping off: branch-name.ts tests the raw template, which is always
truthy, then sets branchTopic to {{{groupSlug}}} — so every security update in the
repo would collapse onto one branch named `renovate/`.
vitest is the only group in this preset whose peers pin to one exact version;
react-dom asks for ^19.2.0 and eslint-config-next for ^7 || ^8 || ^9, and an
ungrouped security PR for either installs fine. @supabase/ssr is a caret range too,
but it raises the floor as it goes, so its security PR installs only if the repo's
supabase-js already meets that floor (see the supabase rule below).
Extend the test below only for a package whose peer range is a single exact version.
The name it emits must stay identical to the vitest groupName in packageRules, or
the pair splits again.
Group routine minor and patch updates into ONE pull request per repo, so a merge to
main leaves one open Renovate PR to rebase instead of one per package. FIRST in this
list on purpose: later rules win, so every named group below (react, eslint, vercel,
supabase, vitest) and any repo's own groupName still beats this one for its packages.
THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO groupSlug HERE. Renovate derives a branch name from the slug
when one is set and from groupName when it is not. A slug set on this rule would NOT
be cleared by the later rules, which set only groupName, so every named group and
every security fix would keep this rule's slug and land on this rule's branch.
With groupName alone each group's branch comes from its own name.
matchManagers IS A POSITIVE LIST, NOT 'everything except github-actions', because the
docs give matchManagers no negation syntax. It leaves out github-actions (action code
runs with repository access and soaks 3 days, so each stays in its own PR where a bad
one is easy to see), nvm and custom managers. A manager not listed keeps its
old behaviour; add it here to group it. majors, pin, pinDigest, digest and
lockFileMaintenance are not matched. Security updates are not grouped by this rule:
vulnerabilityAlerts above is applied as `force` and beats every packageRule.
The cost: one failing package holds every other update in that PR until fixed.
Delete this rule to undo it; the next Renovate run goes back to one PR per package.
Tailwind minor and patch updates keep their own PR instead of joining the grouped one
above. The lockfile update for these packages fails the 'renovate/artifacts' check with
npm error EALLOWREMOTE, leaving package.json changed and the lockfile not. The cause is
known: the hosted Renovate app writes lockfiles with npm 12, and npm 12 refuses the
registry tarball of any package that declares bundleDependencies (npm/cli#9800, still
open; fixes in #9818 and #9819 are not merged; newest npm 12 is 12.2.2).
@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi declares them. In the grouped PR that one failure would
hold every other routine update, so these keep their own. The name is the one
config:recommended (group:tailwindcssMonorepo) gave before the grouped rule existed,
so the branch is again renovate/tailwindcss-monorepo. Majors are not matched and keep
that preset's behaviour. Delete this rule once the Tailwind lockfile update works
again; the packages then join the grouped PR. No groupSlug, for the reason given above.
Tailwind packages use an npm below 12 for the lockfile step, in learn and health only.
That avoids the npm 12 EALLOWREMOTE failure described in the rule above (npm/cli#9800).
Majors are included: there is no matchUpdateTypes here.
THIS NAMES TWO REPOSITORIES ON PURPOSE. An npm below 12 does not refuse dependencies
from URL or git sources when it writes a lockfile. learn and health install in CI with
npm 12.2.2 and an env block that sets allow-remote, allow-git, allow-file and
allow-directory to none and fixes the registry (learn #426, health #59), so a
non-registry source written into a lockfile is refused in CI before the update can merge.
Other repos have no such step and must not get this rule.
The tradeoff: for these packages in these two repos, Renovate's lockfile step runs an npm
that does not itself refuse URL or git sources. The CI install step is what refuses them.
To add a repository, give it the same CI install step first, then add it to the list.
To remove: once npm ships the fix for npm/cli#9800, delete this rule. Then, when Tailwind
updates pass in the grouped pull request, the 'tailwindcss monorepo' rule can go too.
No groupName and no groupSlug: grouping is decided by the rule above.
Group Supabase client packages. @supabase/ssr raises its supabase-js peer floor as it
goes (0.12.7 needs ^2.114.0), so a bump of ssr alone can fail ERESOLVE: learn #385.
KNOWN-LIMITATION(group-supabase-renovate, 2026-11-02): this does not reach two cases. A
security update stays ungrouped (see vulnerabilityAlerts), and a supabase-js major
goes to renovate/major-supabase while an ssr minor stays on renovate/supabase. Either
fails the same way if the ssr version it lands on needs a newer supabase-js.
Group vitest packages. This name must stay identical to the one in the
vulnerabilityAlerts block above — the branch is renovate/{{groupSlug}}, so the
security update and the ordinary one share a PR only while both say 'vitest'.
Change one and you must change the other, or the pair splits again.
Without this rule the name comes from `group:monorepos` and is 'vitest monorepo',
while nicgpt's own renovate.json already calls it 'vitest'. Those two spellings
produced renovate/vitest-monorepo on el-ifs, health and learn and renovate/vitest
on nicgpt, so no single name in the block above could have rejoined the group on
all four repos. Naming it here makes the preset self-sufficient: a repo needs no
vitest rule of its own, and nicgpt's is now a duplicate that agrees.
Hold @vitest/coverage-v8 at 4.1.11 on the two repos caught below it. GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9
lists vitest but not coverage-v8, so the security path takes vitest to the LOWEST
fixed version (4.1.11) while coverage-v8 takes the ordinary path to the latest
(4.1.12). The group above keeps them in one PR but cannot keep them on one version,
and coverage-v8 peers on exactly its own vitest version, so the PR cannot install:
ERESOLVE on health #48 and el-ifs #75. The repo list is deliberate: this rule cannot
see vitest's target, so on a repo with no vitest security update it would itself
split the pair. Delete it once both repos are at 4.1.11 or later; from that version
on it matches nothing.
KNOWN-LIMITATION(GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9, 2026-11-02): this covers this one advisory. A
later vitest CVE whose lowest fix is older than the latest release splits the pair
the same way.
Auto-merge every minor and patch update, in every manager and every depType
(via PR — see the top-level description for why automergeType stays 'pr').
This replaces three narrower rules: 'dependencies' patch, 'devDependencies'
minor + patch, and an explicit automerge:false that held 'dependencies' minors
for manual review.
WHY BLANKET RATHER THAN ENUMERATED. The replaced rules matched on depType, and
the only depTypes they ever named were npm's two. Everything else fell through
with no automerge rule at any level: github-actions emits 'action', 'workflow',
'uses-with', 'github-runner', 'container' and 'service'; gomod emits 'require'
and 'indirect'; npm itself also emits 'optionalDependencies', 'peerDependencies',
'engines' and 'packageManager'. That is what left el-harness #59, el-website #7,
linear-tui #15 and el-admin #194 sitting open for 8-22 days.
AND WHY ONE RULE RATHER THAN A LONGER LIST. Renovate automerges a BRANCH only
when EVERY update on it qualifies. el-admin #194 carried an automergeable
@types/node patch next to a 'uses-with' row that matched nothing, and the one
unmatched row held the whole branch manual. Enumerating depTypes leaves that
failure exactly one unlisted depType away, forever.
Majors are untouched — the dependencyDashboardApproval rule below still holds
them, and 'digest'/'pinDigest' are deliberately NOT auto-merged here: a moved
tag on an already-pinned SHA is the supply-chain case, not a version bump.
NO REPO IS HELD OUT OF THIS RULE ANY MORE. linear-tui was, until 2026-11-16, when its
main got required status checks 'Lint' and 'Test'. The reason it was held out stands
for any future repo with no required check: Renovate merges on the checks it can
see, so when one workflow does not run at all (a path or branch filter, a renamed
workflow or job) and the others pass, Renovate sees only green. GitHub keeps a
REQUIRED check 'pending' in that case and blocks the merge. A required check does
NOT cover a job skipped by its own `if:`: GitHub counts 'skipped' and 'neutral' as
passing too (GitHub docs, 'Troubleshooting required status checks'), so keep `if:`
conditions off required jobs. An earlier version of this note said otherwise.
el-design-system still has no required check; it merges through its own ignoreTests
rule at the end of this list, not through this rule's backstop.

packageRules.description: Auto-merge lock file maintenance (via PR — see top-level description)
Auto-merge pin operations (via PR — see top-level description)
Require dashboard approval for major updates

description: GitHub Actions majors auto-merge on ci. Overrides the blanket major rule above
(later packageRules win), restoring EDR-0062 §6's tiering — 'dev/tooling/actions
-> auto-merge on ci; runtime libs -> dependency-gate; majors -> human'. The blanket
rule was holding actions majors too, which the tiering never intended: an actions
bump changes the CI runner, not shipped code, and ci proves it before merge.
GitHub Actions soak for three days before auto-merging, matching the npm soak
this preset already inherits. config:best-practices pulls in
security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, and EVERY rule in that preset is scoped
matchDatasources: ['npm'] — so actions, which resolve through github-tags,
github-releases and github-digest, had no soak at all and would otherwise
auto-merge a release the same hour it is published.
SCOPED BY matchUpdateTypes ON PURPOSE — DO NOT WIDEN IT. The inherited npm
preset carves minimumReleaseAge back to null for lockFileMaintenance, pin,
replacement, bump, lockfileUpdate and rollback, because those update types have
no release timestamp to age against. Later packageRules win, so a blanket
minimumReleaseAge added here would override those carve-outs — and the failure
is silent, not loud: internalChecksFilter defaults to 'strict' and
minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour to 'timestamp-required', so the update is marked
pending and never raised. No PR, no error, just a dashboard section.
minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour IS SET HERE FOR THAT SAME REASON. The github-runners
datasource is a hardcoded list of runner labels and emits no releaseTimestamp
on any of them, so a runs-on bump has nothing to age against and would stall
under the default. 'timestamp-optional' lets it through with a warning while
still soaking every update that does carry a timestamp.
Majors are out of scope deliberately: they are gated by dashboard approval, and
the actions-majors override above is left exactly as it is.
Restates the inherited carve-outs for the surface the rule above covers, so
that widening that rule cannot resurrect the silent stall described in it.
A no-op today — the soak above does not match these update types — and scoped
to github-actions so it cannot reach the npm soak or the next/react soaks.

packageRules.description: TypeScript does not follow semver — pin exact version

description: dotfiles, el-design-system and learn get the whole of Monday instead of the 4-hour
schedule:earlyMondays window (midnight-4am America/Los_Angeles). Rule added 2026-10-16.
For about 8 weeks Renovate opened ZERO PRs in dotfiles and el-design-system while updates sat
under 'Awaiting Schedule' on their Dependency Dashboards. On 2026-10-16 at 11:48Z
the 'create all awaiting schedule PRs' box was ticked on dotfiles and Renovate
opened 5 PRs (#502-#506) within a minute, so the window is what blocks them.
Busier repos (linear-tui, el-harness, website) do get PRs inside the window.
The likely reason is that the hosted app visits quiet repos too rarely to land
inside a 4-hour weekly slot (the dotfiles dashboard was last refreshed Monday
about 20:08 PDT, well outside it). No other repo's schedule changes.
learn joined this rule on 2026-11-01. Its last routine PR was 2026-10-12. Renovate
rewrote its dashboard at 2026-10-26T11:07:55Z, eight minutes after the window closed,
so Renovate was visiting on that Monday outside the window. That does not prove a
PR would have opened. The dashboard shows no rewrite on 2026-10-19, which settles
nothing: an edit appears only when the body changes.
automergeSchedule is deliberately NOT set: nothing in this preset narrows it for
ordinary updates, so it stays at Renovate's default 'at any time' and cannot
become the new bottleneck. Security PRs are unaffected by this rule wherever it
sits: the vulnerabilityAlerts block is applied as a `force` object that beats
every packageRule (see that block), so they keep schedule 'at any time'.
nicgpt joined this rule on 2026-11-12. Renovate opened exactly two PRs on each of the
five Mondays 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-02 while about 17 updates sat under 'Awaiting
Schedule', including the provider-runtime group last merged 2026-08-24 (#302). The
cause is not proven; the likely one is a single visit inside the window with a
two-PR limit per visit.
el-design-system automerges without waiting for status checks. Nic chose this on
2026-10-16: the repo has no CI at all, so Renovate reads its branch status as
'yellow' (zero checks) and never reaches the 'green' automerge needs. Apps consume
it by vendoring files, not as a package dependency, so a bad bump there cannot
break an app's install or build on its own.
ignoreTests ONLY skips the check wait. It does not turn automerge on: what merges
is still decided by the rules above (minor/patch, lockFileMaintenance, pin and
security updates), and majors stay behind dashboard approval. Kept LAST so no
later rule can override it. Delete it the day el-design-system gets a CI check.
